subject.title: Complementary tool: automated skill quality scoring for curation workflow

question: Should ClawHub endorse/document agent-skill-infra as optional reviewer tooling, integrate vetted quality outputs into curation, or defer until the quality-signal and content-policy RFCs define the trust boundary?
rationale: Automation cannot choose the authority, data-handling policy, and user-facing semantics for model-backed quality scores that may influence security review and moderation.

options.title: Stage a quality-signal contract first
options.body: Define advisory semantics, provider/data handling, provenance, freshness, and separation from ClawScan before any CLI endorsement or integration.

options.title: Document as optional reviewer tooling
options.body: Treat agent-skill-infra as an external manual aid only, with clear non-endorsement and no stored trust impact.

options.title: Integrate vetted outputs
options.body: Accept quality results into ClawHub only after adding schema/API/UI boundaries, security review, and compatibility tests for score provenance.

recommendation.title: Stage a quality-signal contract first
recommendation.body: Define advisory semantics, provider/data handling, provenance, freshness, and separation from ClawScan before any CLI endorsement or integration.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the CODEOWNERS-listed reviewer for the backend, scan, CLI, moderation, and security-doc surfaces that would own this decision.
